problem: Modular ObjectNav pipelines (segmentation-based semantic mapping, dense goal prediction, planning) are too slow and memory-hungry for edge devices. The usual fix of shrinking backbones costs a lot of navigation quality and ignores temporal redundancy and map sparsity.
motivation: Profiling a PEANUT agent on Jetson Orin shows semantic mapping takes 83% of per-step latency (482 ms) and the goal-prediction model takes 79% of the 3,519 MB peak memory. Consecutive observations are redundant and the semantic map is under 10% non-zero, so deployment gains can come from scheduling perception and sparse encoding instead of uniform model shrinking.
key_idea: Use a learned depth-histogram-based scheduler (SKIP) to skip semantic segmentation on redundant FORWARD steps, and a sparse+lightweight-dense goal-prediction encoder (SCOUT) to cut memory and compute, jointly forming a device-aware Pareto design space.
insight: A strong backbone scheduled sparsely beats a weak backbone run every step: at about 88% skip SKIP loses about 3.6% SPL, versus 10-24% for ESANet/SegFormer swaps and 19-23% for periodic/L1/JS heuristics at matched skip. For SCOUT, sparse-only (0.252) and dense-only with context (0.281) both underperform, while sparse R50 plus dense R18 context reaches 0.361 on the 200-episode ablation, so the interaction is what matters. SKIP also acts as a semantic noise filter, raising SPL in hard episodes and slightly lowering it in easy ones.
method: SKIP map-impact criterion: a step is safe to skip if the L1 distance between consecutive single-frame projections, L_m(t), is below tau; the scheduler is applied only on FORWARD steps and turns always segment.

Skip predictor J_theta: a random-forest classifier on the 50-bin depth-histogram difference, trained on labels from 200 HM3D training episodes; the step is skipped iff P(safe) > c, and it runs in about 1.6 ms.
Depth-map retention: obstacle and explored-area channels are always updated from depth, so only the semantic layers lag.
SCOUT sparse stream: a SparseResNet-50 with submanifold sparse convolutions and strided sparse blocks that compute only on active map cells.
SCOUT dense context stream: a lightweight ResNet-18 on a pooled, down-sampled map, fused with the sparse features at two points (F1, F2) before a PSPNet decode head, plus a train-only auxiliary head.

Device-aware configuration selection: profile latency, memory and energy for each (segmentation backbone, skip policy, goal encoder) configuration, discard those violating device budgets, and pick the max-SPL feasible one.

setting.backbone: Mask R-CNN R-101 (or ESANet/SegFormer) segmentation + SCOUT (SparseResNet-50 + ResNet-18, PSPNet head) goal predictor + random-forest skip predictor, with FMM planning
setting.training_data: SCOUT trained on the PEANUT protocol on HM3D; skip predictor trained on 200 HM3D training episodes; retrained ESANet/SegFormer baselines
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D; Gibson for the PONI transfer study)

results: On HM3D ObjectNav, SCOUT alone improves SPL from 30.8 (PEANUT) to 33.3 on VAL. SKIP+SCOUT keeps 33.0 SPL and reaches 34.3 SPL on TEST-STANDARD, beating PEANUT's 33.0. It gives 1.6-1.7x speedup (Orin 482→283 ms), 50.5% lower peak memory (3,519→1,743 MB) and 47% lower per-frame energy. Naive backbone shrinking loses 10.4% (ESANet) to 24.4% (SegFormer) SPL.
limitations: Only the modular PEANUT/PONI ObjectNav pipelines are studied, and planning is not optimized; all evaluation is in simulation without real-robot deployment.
Robustness is tested only for zero-mean Gaussian depth noise, not for depth dropout, holes, or bias.
Skipping costs SPL in easy episodes, and the skip predictor and tau/c need per-backbone or per-pipeline tuning.
